topic: Lambda Capture Scoping: Closure Member vs. Local Variable
explanation: When using generalized capture syntax `[ lhs = rhs ]`, the scoping rules are crucial: the identifier on the left-hand side (`lhs`) refers to a data member of the compiler-generated closure class, while the expression on the right-hand side (`rhs`) is evaluated in the scope where the lambda is defined (the outer scope). This separation allows for effective resource transfer, even when the data member is given the same name as the local variable (e.g., `[ pw = std::move(pw) ]`), where the left `pw` is the closure member and the right `pw` is the local variable.
practical_example: A developer attempts to capture a local variable by value using generalized capture but mistakenly assumes the `rhs` is evaluated in the closure scope, leading to confusion about when the initialization occurs and which variable name is being referenced inside the lambda body.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
